thread:
Maria Lopez: Heads up — we've got a customer escalation (INC-6421) reporting a sharp spike in 5xx from the hosted API since ~10:02 UTC in us-west-2. Multiple paying customers impacted. :warning:
SRE Bot: Alert: 5xx rate increased across api-router.* in us-west-2 (10:05 UTC). Spike from 0.3% -> ~6%.
Alex Chen: I'm on it. Any deploys or config changes in the last 20m?
Jamal Ortiz: We rolled a canary hotpatch at 09:58 — feature flag `route_pref_override=true` to 5% canary. Next step was automatic ramp to 25% at 10:10.
Olivia Park: Reassigning oncall -> @Priya. Priya Rao (Oncall): I'm here, looking now.
Priya Rao: Reproducing with curl from an external client (us-west):
Priya Rao: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'`
Priya Rao: Response: 502, body: `{"error":"gateway timeout"}`.
Priya Rao: Log snippet: ```ERROR api-router: proxy to upstream 10.4.2.12:8080 EOF while proxying request; conn reset by peer; request_id=xyz123```
Alex Chen: Could the hotpatch change routing headers/tag selection? The patch touched `route_tag` logic last minute.
Maria Lopez: Support is seeing some 401s turning into 500s too — customers losing traffic and usage is dropping for a few accounts. Billing team wants to know if invoices affected.
Support Bot: INC-6421 attached. Customer says every request returns 502 starting 10:03 UTC; they gave sample request IDs.
Jamal Ortiz: Looking at the hotpatch history: `hotpatch/2026-03-17-0958` patched `route_tag` but I see a typo in the value: it wrote `legazy` instead of `legacy`. That would fail tag lookups.
Olivia Park: If router receives an unknown tag it may fallthrough to a default backend pool that isn't healthy — matches the EOFs.
Alex Chen: We need to stop the rollout. Jamal, can you halt and revert the canary to 0%? Priya, coordinate rollback and runbook.
Jamal Ortiz: Reverting now: `orbctl rollout set canary 0 --change-id hotpatch/2026-03-17-0958` :eyes:
SRE Bot: Deploy controller: rollback initiated for change hotpatch/2026-03-17-0958.
Priya Rao: Following runbook: disable flag at canary scope: `cfgctl patch feature route_pref_override=false --env=prod --scope=canary` then verify routing table.
Priya Rao: Flag disabled and canary traffic reverted. Checking metrics...
Priya Rao: 5xx rate dropping: ~6% -> 1.2% within 3m. Continuing to monitor. :white_check_mark:
Maria Lopez: Drafting customer message: "We identified a configuration hotpatch with a mistyped routing tag causing requests to route to an unhealthy backend. We've rolled back the change and service is recovering. We're following up with a postmortem."
Billing Bot: Billing queue notified. No invoice changes detected yet; we'll reconcile any missed usage logs once stability confirmed.
Alex Chen: Action items: 1) Postmortem covering automation that allowed typo (Jamal), 2) Add schema validation for `route_tag` values in hotpatch pipeline, 3) Add canary guardrail: block automatic ramp beyond 10% if healthchecks flag shows anomaly.
Jamal Ortiz: I'll own the hotpatch pipeline fix and add validation tests.
Olivia Park: I'll open the incident postmortem doc and schedule follow-up 1pm PT.
Priya Rao: Will keep the incident open until 30m of stable 5xx < 0.5% and customer confirms. Monitoring looks healthy so far.
Maria Lopez: Thanks team — I'll send the customer update and mark INC-6421 with recovery. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: Good recovery. Note for PMs: avoid shortcuts that bypass config validation in hotpatches.
SRE Bot: Monitoring: 5xx back to baseline over last 8 minutes. Incident transitioning to monitoring/after-action.
